item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-43a55b6186573a07","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The WFP-led evaluation of the Joint Resilience Programme in the DRC found that the programme’s multisectoral approach addressed vulnerable communities’ needs, but logistical complexity meant only 50% of planned activities were fully implemented.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evaluation was conducted during 2023–2024 and covered a programme running from 2018 to 2024; it provides partial evidence relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The programme operated in the DRC during Tshisekedi’s presidency, but the source does not establish that the president personally designed or controlled its implementation.","limitations":["The finding concerns a multisectoral programme involving WFP, UNICEF, FAO, and other implementers, not exclusively the national government."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43a55b6186573a07","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The evaluation attributed significant improvements in water, sanitation, and hygiene facilities at health centers and schools to the Joint Resilience Programme, while access to improved sanitation and water sources remained generally low.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evaluation was conducted during 2023–2024 and reports programme effects over a multi-year period including 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns a programme implemented in the DRC under the national context, but does not isolate Tshisekedi’s personal contribution.","limitations":["The source does not provide national-level coverage or a president-specific causal estimate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43a55b6186573a07","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Households with women participating in village savings and loan associations had higher food-consumption and dietary-diversity scores and grew more crops; trained smallholders reported increased yields and use of crops for household consumption and sale.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evaluation covered a programme operating through 2023; the page does not date these outcomes to a specific month.","ruler_attribution":"The outcomes are associated with the Joint Resilience Programme and its implementing agencies, not specifically with Tshisekedi.","limitations":["Reported outcomes are programme-level findings and may not generalize nationally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43a55b6186573a07","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The three implementing agencies maintained dedicated monitoring and evaluation teams and regular field missions, but their monitoring efforts had limited coordination and alignment.","question_ids":["6B.5","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evaluation covered 2018–2024 and was conducted in 2023–2024.","ruler_attribution":"This is an institutional finding about the implementing agencies; the source does not attribute the coordination failure to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["No evidence is provided about presidential direction, correction, or resourcing of the monitoring system."]},{"source_id":"SRC-43a55b6186573a07","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The evaluation recommended activity layering, a stronger focus on accessibility and sustainability including government ownership, expanded peacebuilding coverage, aligned monitoring strategies, community-level NGO coordination, and more transparent communication about targeting and women’s access to credit.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"These are recommendations issued from an evaluation conducted during 2023–2024.","ruler_attribution":"The recommendations identify institutional needs but do not establish whether Tshisekedi adopted or implemented them during 2023.","limitations":["Recommendations are not evidence of completed government action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-71938663304f882d","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"An ICRC evaluation completed in November 2022 found that the Surgical Learning Hub in Bukavu provided structured training for local, national, and international health workers and onboarding for ICRC surgical teams; it recommended strengthening the model while noting that local enabling conditions might not exist elsewhere and that relationship-building and partnership investment would be needed.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.9","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evaluation was completed in 2022 and published in 2023, so it provides limited direct evidence for the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The hub was an ICRC initiative; the source does not attribute its establishment or performance to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["This is an external humanitarian institution’s project evaluation, not a national-government performance assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd43ebebc8dbfa79","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A doctoral research project examined Tshisekedi’s 2018–2023 presidential State of the Nation speeches as instruments for structuring power, legitimizing authority, mobilizing citizens, responding to international pressures, and articulating a national vision.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The research explicitly covers Tshisekedi’s first mandate from 2018 to 2023, including the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly concerns Tshisekedi’s presidential speeches, but reports the study’s subject and aims rather than its completed empirical findings.","limitations":["No specific speech, policy commitment, or verified implementation result is provided on the page."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fd34b5842dd9ba9a","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A UN-led group of agencies recorded more than 12,600 cases of sexual violence in North Kivu between January and March; the ICRC described sexual violence as a major protection issue despite prohibition under national and international law.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article was published in 2024 and reports a January–March count without specifying the year in the supplied text; it therefore has uncertain direct fit to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns conditions in the DRC and armed actors generally; it does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal responsibility.","limitations":["The reported period is not explicitly identified as 2023 in the supplied units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fd34b5842dd9ba9a","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The ICRC reported that more than half of women in the DRC had been exposed to some form of physical violence and that more than 27% reported sexual violence in armed conflict; it also linked increased sexual violence to intensified hostilities, fragmentation of armed actors, displacement, and resource scarcity.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article is from 2024 and presents broader conflict-related conditions rather than a measure confined to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies armed conflict and structural conditions, not a president-specific causal effect.","limitations":["The statistics are not dated to 2023 and do not distinguish state from non-state perpetrators."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fd34b5842dd9ba9a","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the ICRC provided mental-health and psychological-support services to 3,233 survivors and victims of sexual violence in the DRC through listening houses, referrals to health facilities, medical support, and needs-based financial assistance.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly dated to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The services were provided by the ICRC with support from the local DRC Red Cross; the source does not show that Tshisekedi’s government funded, directed, or implemented them.","limitations":["This measures humanitarian assistance, not national-government protection or prosecution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6f0b7d1b31b92f02","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"On May 20, police violently dispersed a peaceful opposition march in Kinshasa, arrested dozens, and seriously injured at least 30 people; police said they opened an investigation and arrested three officers for beating a child, while Tshisekedi publicly congratulated the police chief who oversaw the operation and praised the dispersal.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly dated to May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the public praise to Tshisekedi and identifies the operation as occurring under his government.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and official statements; the completeness and independence of the investigation are not established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6f0b7d1b31b92f02","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Videos showed police and civilians beating peaceful demonstrators, including a child, with wooden sticks; three police officers were arrested for brutalizing demonstrators and a minor, while the human rights minister condemned the violence and called for an urgent investigation.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly dated to the May 20, 2023 protest and subsequent official response.","ruler_attribution":"The arrests and ministerial condemnation were actions by Tshisekedi’s government; the source does not establish whether the president ordered or corrected the abuses beyond his praise for the police chief.","limitations":["The source does not report the final findings or sanctions from the investigation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-767dfe118a73fc35","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented election-related clashes since early October that caused assaults, sexual violence, and at least one death; supporters of Tshisekedi’s UDPS were implicated in threats and attacks against opposition leaders and journalists, and more than 1.5 million people in conflict areas were expected to be unable to vote.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","4B.1","4B.3","4B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the October–December 2023 electoral period.","ruler_attribution":"The source implicates UDPS supporters and describes state obligations, but does not establish that Tshisekedi personally directed the reported attacks.","limitations":["The account includes violence by both ruling-party and opposition supporters; attribution varies by incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-767dfe118a73fc35","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In Kasumbalesa on November 7, UDPS supporters attacked opposition supporters, injuring six people, raping at least two women, and sexually assaulting three others; the authorities were not known to have investigated the reported physical and sexual violence.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly dated to November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The perpetrators were identified as supporters of Tshisekedi’s UDPS, but the source does not establish presidential direction; it reports an absence of known investigation by authorities.","limitations":["The source relies on witness, security, medical, and UN sources and does not report final judicial findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-767dfe118a73fc35","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"During the 2023 campaign, journalists were detained, threatened, or denied access: intelligence agents arrested journalist Raphael Ngoma without charge; John Kanyunyu Kyota received threats and went into hiding; journalists were denied airport access; and security forces reportedly followed instructions from Kinshasa to restrict coverage of an opposition candidate.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns November–December 2023 campaign events.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes some actions to intelligence agents and security forces and reports alleged instructions from Kinshasa, but does not identify Tshisekedi as the direct issuer.","limitations":["The alleged chain of command is not independently established in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-767dfe118a73fc35","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"A provincial governor’s campaign SUV apparently bearing campaign advertisements and a UDPS flag struck and killed an opposition youth leader in Kindu; two arrests were made, but the investigation was reportedly stalling because of alleged political interference and the family was denied autopsy results.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly dated to November 28, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The vehicle was linked to a provincial governor’s campaign team and carried a UDPS flag; the source does not establish presidential involvement.","limitations":["The account reports allegations and judicial-source information rather than a completed finding of responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-767dfe118a73fc35","start_unit":18,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"The CSAC banned broadcast of a UDPS provincial governor’s statement that only Tshisekedi’s home province should receive votes, finding that it incited ethnic-regional hatred, exclusion, and discrimination.","question_ids":["3B.3","4B.3","4B.6","4B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly dated to October 24, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statement was made by a UDPS provincial governor and referred to Tshisekedi; the source does not show that Tshisekedi authored or endorsed it, and records a regulatory response by CSAC.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether Tshisekedi disciplined or otherwise responded to the governor."]},{"source_id":"SRC-767dfe118a73fc35","start_unit":18,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"The EU cancelled its countrywide election-observation mission after Congolese authorities did not authorize satellite equipment for deployment and sent only an eight-person expert mission to Kinshasa; civil-society groups said the decision created the impression of a hidden electoral agenda.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 election period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the authorization decision to Congolese authorities but does not identify Tshisekedi’s personal role.","limitations":["The source reports civil-society interpretation of the decision rather than a judicial or independent finding of electoral manipulation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80c399a5687c1975","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated the DRC Not Free with a score of 19/100 and described the political system as paralyzed by manipulation of the electoral process, with citizens unable to freely exercise basic civil liberties and physical security threatened by government forces, rebel groups, and militias.","question_ids":["3B.6","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report is the 2023 edition but its key developments primarily concern 2022; it is partial contextual evidence for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment covers the Tshisekedi administration but is country-level and does not isolate his personal decisions.","limitations":["Aggregate country rating and overview do not provide a single 2023 event or direct causal attribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80c399a5687c1975","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Freedom House found that opposition prospects were impaired by postponed elections, government interference, and disruptions; military and security forces hindered political participation; corruption was extensive; and the government lacked transparency over finances, extractive contracts, and state involvement in violence.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.7","5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 edition chiefly reports conditions and developments through 2022, so the evidence is partial for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the national government during Tshisekedi’s presidency but do not establish that he personally caused each condition.","limitations":["The report combines institutional and historical evidence and is not limited to the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80c399a5687c1975","start_unit":8,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reported that journalists faced threats, detention, arbitrary arrest, and physical attacks; open dissent was routinely suppressed; demonstrations exposed participants to arrest and violence; the judiciary was politically manipulated; arbitrary detention and prolonged pretrial detention were common; and reparations formally granted to victims were rarely paid.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 edition primarily describes conditions through 2022, with limited direct fit to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern state institutions under Tshisekedi’s administration but do not establish his personal involvement in each practice.","limitations":["Country-level assessment; most examples are not dated within 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80c399a5687c1975","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reported persistent discrimination against women, ethnic minorities, Indigenous peoples, people with disabilities, and LGBT+ people; it also reported widespread sexual and gender-based violence, rare convictions, forced labor, and child recruitment by government forces and armed groups.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 edition chiefly assesses conditions through 2022 and is contextual rather than a 2023-specific measurement.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern national laws and practices during Tshisekedi’s presidency but do not isolate his personal responsibility.","limitations":["The source does not quantify change during 2023 or distinguish all state from non-state perpetrators."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7089c4d34f50e75d","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"The 2023 election-observation mission reported that voting rights were extended to citizens in the diaspora in South Africa, the United States, France, and Belgium, but identified inadequate polling infrastructure and accessibility, especially for people with disabilities and older people.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.7","6B.8","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 20, 2023 elections.","ruler_attribution":"The election framework and administration were state responsibilities during Tshisekedi’s presidency, but the source does not attribute each decision personally to him.","limitations":["The supplied abstract does not provide the mission’s full findings or quantify the effects of diaspora voting."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7089c4d34f50e75d","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"The election-observation mission reported long queues, alleged registration irregularities, closed registration centers, uneven distribution of enrollment machines, shortages of voting kits, communication failures by CENI officials, user-unfriendly voting procedures, insufficient ballot-secrecy guarantees, technical glitches, and malfunctioning voting devices.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.7","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election cycle and election day.","ruler_attribution":"These are findings about CENI and the election administration under Tshisekedi’s government; the source does not establish presidential personal control over each operational failure.","limitations":["The abstract reports alleged irregularities and operational problems but does not determine their intent or legal consequences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7aac5524c3ce4928","start_unit":12,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that at least seven journalists had been harassed or attacked by political actors in Kinshasa and Kananga since early July 2023, while one journalist faced a criminal defamation case; it recorded a July attack on a press vehicle, other assaults by opposition supporters, and a possible five-year prison sentence for Pascal Kamanzi.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns July–August 2023 pre-election events.","ruler_attribution":"The attacks involved political actors from different sides; the government condemned one attack and promised an investigation, but the source does not attribute the incidents directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not report completed investigations or prosecutions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7aac5524c3ce4928","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"RSF gave the DRC a press-freedom score of 42.16 and rank 130 of 180 in its 2023 index.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The index was published on August 21, 2023 and is directly relevant to the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The index assesses the country during Tshisekedi’s presidency but does not attribute the score to a specific presidential act.","limitations":["An aggregate index does not identify individual policies or causal mechanisms."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fb749af23b7c4538","start_unit":12,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that during the November 19–December 18, 2023 presidential campaign at least five journalists were threatened or attacked by politicians or supporters, reporters were denied access to public places and airports, and authorities were urged not to cut internet access during or after the election.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 presidential campaign and election.","ruler_attribution":"The incidents involved ruling-party supporters, opposition actors, politicians, and security forces; the source calls on Congolese authorities but does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal orders.","limitations":["The article reports allegations and calls for action rather than final adjudications."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fb749af23b7c4538","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"RSF stated that Tshisekedi’s five-year term had been marked by three journalist murders, two enforced disappearances, many death threats, and at least 123 arbitrary arrests, including the continued detention of Stanis Bujakera; only three of 24 presidential candidates had signed RSF’s press-freedom commitments.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published December 20, 2023 and explicitly assesses Tshisekedi’s presidential term, including the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly evaluates the press-freedom record during Tshisekedi’s term but does not assert that he personally ordered each abuse.","limitations":["The supplied text does not provide case-by-case findings or distinguish state from non-state perpetrators for all incidents."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-97db90a40c7c9b1e","SRC-dd48aa36708db26a"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents contain little direct evidence about nuclear, arms-control, proliferation, macroeconomic, fiscal, or personal-financial conduct during 2023.","Several institutional reports describe national or partner-programme conditions without isolating Félix Tshisekedi’s personal authority, decisions, or causal contribution.","Some 2023-edition reports primarily summarize 2022 conditions; their period fit is therefore partial where noted."]}
